subject.title: [Bug]: browser in docker hidden in cache folder

question: Should Docker browser-enabled images keep /home/node/.cache/ms-playwright with runtime autodetection, or migrate browser assets to /opt and add stable chrome/chromium PATH commands?
rationale: Current source, docs, tests, and the latest release encode the home-cache contract, while prior /opt attempts exposed compatibility and proof gaps that automation should not settle as a product choice.

options.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
options.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave /opt plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

options.title: Approve /opt Plus PATH Migration
options.body: Require a focused Dockerfile/docs/test change with live proof for browser-enabled, browser-disabled, runtime-install, and existing-cache upgrade scenarios.

options.title: Narrow To PATH Aliases
options.body: Keep the current cache location but add layout-aware chrome and chromium aliases only if maintainers want that Docker command surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
recommendation.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave /opt plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment on the prior same-repository implementation is the clearest product-boundary signal for this Docker path change.
